hints.title: Solitary Bit Observation
hints.text: Powers of two have a distinct representation in binary arithmetic with exactly a single bit turned on. How does subtracting one from a positive power of two change its bit pattern?

hints.title: Lowest Bit Clearing Identity
hints.text: Subtracting one from a power of two flips the lowest set bit and all trailing zero bits to ones. Performing a bitwise conjunction with the original value clears that single bit.

hints.title: Single Bit Conjunction Evaluation
hints.text: Check that the number is strictly positive. Then evaluate the bitwise conjunction of n and n minus one. If the result equals zero, return true; otherwise return false.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(1) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Iterative division by two takes O(log N) operations and requires handling zero and negative boundary conditions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The bitwise identity n & (n - 1) executes in O(1) time and requires zero additional memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should provide the one-line bitwise trick and remember that non-positive integers cannot be powers of two.
